says: The repository says WAL and the person's own decisions say a rollback journal, so a use relying on the journal mode needs their answer. The working host is Claude Code 2.1.278 on MCP 2025-11-25, whose one Elicitation hook is kept disabled; Codex CLI 0.155.1, offering only 2025-06-18, is also installed. A native-form link to each is opened. Each probe runs for real and writes the configuration it ran under: on Claude Code the form reached the person and came back, and the user event separated their submission from automation, so its profile qualifies question and user_event by those probes. Codex declares form support but its real probe declines in milliseconds with nobody present, so its profile says probe_failed: a declaration or protocol qualifies nothing. The owner seals the question against the two choices and stores it pending before asking. Asking through Codex at a version it does not offer is recorded unsupported, protocol_version_not_offered, no channel. In the Claude Code form the person first cancels (a cancelled non-answer); then, while the hook is switched on, the form returns a choice with no separation evidence, and the configuration measured at classification shows the enabled hook, so it is hook_generated. Resuming with either is blocked with answer_not_from_a_person; the same use stays pending_user on the same question version and nothing is admitted. With the hook off again the person chooses WAL, and the owner records a verified_native_user_event answer bound to this link, use, question version and host, under the configuration measured then and naming the real user-event probe as its separation. Resuming the use with it admits it on the unchanged basis and returns the WAL unit.
